info.title: GoBTC Pay Wallet API
info.description:
# GoBTC Pay — Wallet API

This API lets a non-custodial **web3 wallet** integrate GoBTC Pay so its
users can accept and pay for Bitcoin purchases at a merchant's point of
sale. The wallet holds the keys; GoBTC Pay builds the transactions the
wallet signs. A typical integration follows four steps:

1. **[Authenticate](#authentication)** the user with their wallet key.
2. **[Register the wallet](#wallet-setup)** to provision their multisig wallet.
3. **[Read balances](#balances-and-addresses)** to show funds and the wallet address.
4. **[Pay at a POS](#paying-at-a-pos)** by scanning a QR code and signing the payment.

Every authenticated request carries a short-lived **Bearer JWT** obtained
from the challenge–signature flow below.

## Authentication

The wallet proves control of its key by signing a server-issued challenge,
then exchanges the signature for an access / refresh token pair:

1. Call **Get sign-in challenge** with the user's public key. The response
   contains the data to sign (`messageToSign`).
2. Sign that data with the corresponding **private key**.
3. Submit the signature to **Get access tokens** to receive an `accessToken`
   and a `refreshToken`.
4. Send every authenticated request with `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.
5. When the access token expires, get a fresh pair via **Refresh access tokens**.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant W as Wallet app
  participant G as Gateway
  W->>G: Get sign-in challenge (public key)
  G-->>W: messageToSign
  W->>W: sign messageToSign with private key
  W->>G: Get access tokens (signature)
  G-->>W: accessToken + refreshToken
  W->>G: API call (Authorization: Bearer accessToken)
  W->>G: Refresh access tokens (refreshToken)
  G-->>W: new accessToken + refreshToken
```

## Wallet setup

Once authenticated, call **Register wallet** with the user's public key.
GoBTC Pay provisions and returns the user's **multisig wallet** — this is
the user's main wallet, and every payment is spent from it. Call this once,
after generating the key pair.

## Balances and addresses

- **Get balances** — the wallet's balances broken down by state (on-chain,
  signed, locked, spendable), with optional fiat conversion.
- **Get wallet address** — the user's multisig wallet address.

## Paying at a POS

When the user scans the QR code shown on a merchant's POS terminal:

1. Call **Get payment** with the payment id from the QR code, and show the
   user the payment details (amount, merchant, expiry).
2. Call **Build payment transaction** with that payment. The response
   returns a `psbtBase64` — the unsigned transaction. Present it so the user
   can review what they are signing.
3. The user signs the PSBT with their key. Submit the signed transaction via
   **Settle payment** to complete the payment.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant W as Wallet app
  participant G as Gateway
  participant P as POS terminal
  P-->>U: show payment QR
  U->>W: scan QR (paymentId)
  W->>G: Get payment (paymentId)
  G-->>W: payment details
  W->>U: show amount & merchant
  W->>G: Build payment transaction (paymentId)
  G-->>W: psbtBase64
  W->>U: review & sign
  W->>G: Settle payment (signed PSBT)
  G-->>W: paymentTxId
```

---

This is the **Wallet** surface of the GoBTC Pay API. Backwards compatibility is preserved across published versions.

Found an error in the docs? Email [support@gomining.com](mailto:support@gomining.com).

merchantAuth.description: Merchant dashboard access token obtained from `/merchant/auth/login` (or the OAuth / passkey / 2FA login flows). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. Refresh it via `/merchant/auth/refresh` when it expires.

walletAuth.description: Wallet access token obtained from `/instant/auth/get-jwt` via the signature challenge flow. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. Refresh it via `/instant/auth/refresh-jwt` when it expires.

post.description: Starts the authentication challenge. Returns a one-time `messageToSign` and a `challengeId` bound to the supplied public key (valid until `expiresAt`, ~5 min). Sign `messageToSign` verbatim with the corresponding private key using Bitcoin message signing (secp256k1 ECDSA), then exchange it for tokens via **Get access tokens**.

userPubKeyHex.description: Public key of the user's Bitcoin wallet to authenticate — compressed secp256k1 key, hex (33 bytes / 66 chars).

challengeId.description: Unique id of this challenge. Pass it back to **Get access tokens** together with your signature.

messageToSign.description: Message to sign verbatim with the wallet private key (Bitcoin message signing, secp256k1).

expiresAt.description: When the challenge expires, Unix timestamp (seconds). Sign and submit before this time (~5 min).

x-codeSamples.label: JavaScript

post.description: Completes the authentication challenge. Submit the `challengeId` from **Get sign-in challenge** together with the hex-encoded 64-byte compact `signature` of `messageToSign`. Returns a short-lived `accessToken` (send it as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`) and a long-lived `refreshToken`.

signature.description: Hex-encoded 64-byte compact signature of the `messageToSign` from **Get sign-in challenge**.

accessToken.description: Short-lived JWT access token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` on authenticated requests.

refreshToken.description: Long-lived JWT refresh token. Use it at **Refresh access tokens** to obtain a new token pair.

x-codeSamples.label: JavaScript

post.description: Exchanges a valid refresh token for a fresh `accessToken` / `refreshToken` pair without repeating the signing challenge. Send the refresh token as `Authorization: Bearer <refreshToken>` with an empty body.

accessToken.description: Short-lived JWT access token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` on authenticated requests.

refreshToken.description: Long-lived JWT refresh token. Use it at **Refresh access tokens** to obtain a new token pair.

post.description: Registers the user's wallet public key and provisions their multisig wallet — the user's main wallet that all payments are spent from. Call this once after generating the key pair; returns the multisig `address`.

userPubKeyHex.description: Public key of the user's Bitcoin wallet — compressed secp256k1 key, hex (33 bytes). Becomes a signer of the new multisig wallet.

address.description: The user's newly provisioned multisig wallet address.

post.description: Returns the authenticated user's multisig wallet `address`.

Returns the wallet's balances broken down by state — on-chain (confirmed / unconfirmed), signed, locked, pending change, the spendable `leftBalance` and `totalBalance` — all in satoshis. `leftBalance` is `confirmedOnChainBalance - lockedBalance - signedBalance` (floored at 0) and the reservation buckets never overlap; `totalBalance` additionally includes `pendingChangeBalance` — our own change from an already broadcast but still unconfirmed transaction, which is not spendable yet. `leftBalanceInUsd` / `leftBalanceInCurrency` give the fiat equivalent (null when a rate is unavailable). Pass `currency` to choose the fiat conversion.

currency.description: Optional fiat currency for the converted balance fields (e.g. `USD`).

onChainBalance.description: Total balance seen on-chain (confirmed + unconfirmed), in satoshis.

confirmedOnChainBalance.description: On-chain balance with at least one confirmation, in satoshis.

unconfirmedOnChainBalance.description: Net mempool delta for the wallet address (incoming 0-conf outputs minus the value of its inputs spent by mempool txs), in satoshis. Can be negative right after an outgoing transaction — do NOT add it to `confirmedOnChainBalance`, use `pendingChangeBalance` / `totalBalance` for pending funds.

signedBalance.description: Outgoing amount + fee of transactions the user has already signed that are not yet connected into the UTXO graph and hold no UTXO lock, in satoshis. Funds reserved by a lock are reported under `lockedBalance` instead, so the two buckets never overlap.

lockedBalance.description: Balance locked in pending payments / withdrawals (unspent outputs with an active UTXO lock), in satoshis.

pendingChangeBalance.description: Our own change from broadcast but still unconfirmed transactions (e.g. the change of a withdrawal), in satoshis. Not yet spendable, so it is excluded from `leftBalance` and included in `totalBalance`.

leftBalance.description: Spendable balance available for new transactions, in satoshis: sum of confirmed unlocked outputs minus `signedBalance`, floored at 0. Note that `confirmedOnChainBalance` still counts locked outputs, so `leftBalance` is not simply `confirmedOnChainBalance - lockedBalance - signedBalance`.

totalBalance.description: `leftBalance + pendingChangeBalance`, in satoshis — everything the wallet owns and is not spending, including change that is still waiting for a confirmation.

leftBalanceInUsd.description: `leftBalance` converted to USD (null if no rate is available).

leftBalanceInCurrency.description: `leftBalance` converted to the requested `currency` (null if no rate is available).

post.description: Returns the current state of a payment by `paymentId`, including its `status`, amounts, merchant / POS details, and `qrString`. Poll this to track a payment until it is paid or expired.

post.description: Builds the unsigned PSBT that settles a payment. Pass the `paymentId`; the response returns a `jobId`, the `psbtBase64` to sign with the wallet key, and a `summary` of inputs, fee, and change. Sign it client-side, then submit via **Settle payment**.

post.description: Returns everything needed to build a withdrawal PSBT client-side: the multisig descriptor (`m`/`n`, witness script), spendable UTXOs, recommended fee rates (low / medium / high), change script details, and virtual-size parameters for fee estimation.

m.description: Number of required signatures (the *m* in m-of-n multisig).

n.description: Total number of signers (the *n* in m-of-n multisig).

witnessScript.description: Witness script of the multisig wallet, hex-encoded.

vout.description: Index of the referenced output within its transaction.

utxos.description: Spendable UTXOs of the wallet, for building the withdrawal client-side.

feeRateSatVb.description: Fee rate in satoshis per virtual byte (sat/vB).

dustThreshold.description: Minimum output value in satoshis; change below this is treated as dust and dropped.

vSizeP2wsh20f3In.description: Virtual size added per 2-of-3 P2WSH input, in vbytes.

vSizeP2wpkhOut.description: Virtual size added per P2WPKH output, in vbytes.

vSizeP2wshOut.description: Virtual size added per P2WSH output, in vbytes.

post.description: Builds an unsigned withdrawal PSBT to `toAddress`. Provide either `amountSats` or `sendMax`, plus a `fee.feeRateSatVb`. Optionally pin inputs with `selectUtxos` and enable replace-by-fee with `rbf`. Returns the `jobId`, `psbtBase64`, and a `summary` (fee, vsize, change, inputs). Co-sign, then submit via **Broadcast withdrawal**.

toAddress.description: Destination Bitcoin address for the funds.

sendMax.description: If true, sweeps the entire spendable balance to `toAddress` and ignores the amount.

feeRateSatVb.description: Fee rate in satoshis per virtual byte (sat/vB).

vout.description: Index of the referenced output within its transaction.

selectUtxos.description: Optional list of specific UTXOs to spend. If omitted, coins are selected automatically.

rbf.description: Enable Replace-By-Fee (BIP-125) so the transaction can be fee-bumped later.

jobId.description: Id of this withdrawal build. Pass it with the co-signed PSBT to **Broadcast withdrawal**.

psbtBase64.description: Unsigned transaction as a base64-encoded PSBT (BIP-174). Sign it with the wallet key.

toAddress.description: Destination Bitcoin address for the funds.

feeSats.description: Network fee for the transaction, in satoshis.

feeRateSatVb.description: Fee rate in satoshis per virtual byte (sat/vB).

vsize.description: Estimated virtual size of the transaction, in vbytes.

vout.description: Index of the referenced output within its transaction.

post.description: Broadcasts a co-signed withdrawal. Submit the `jobId` from **Build withdrawal PSBT** and the `signedPsbtBase64`. Returns the broadcast `txid` (and `txHex` when available).

txHex.description: Raw signed transaction, hex-encoded (available once broadcast).

post.description: Returns the parameters a client needs to work with BTC locally: `network` (mainnet / testnet), `nativeSymbol` and `nativeDecimals`, the default derivation path, the dust threshold in satoshis, and explorer URL templates for addresses and transactions (both contain `{value}` for the client to substitute). These describe the INSTALLATION — one deployment serves exactly one network — so there is no chain or token registry to query.

Creates a self-custody wallet for the public key in the JWT. The private key never reaches the server. One public key maps to at most one wallet: calling this again returns the existing `walletId` with `created: false` and does NOT overwrite `name`. A freshly registered wallet has no addresses — add them with `/selfcustody/address/add`.

Returns the wallet of the authenticated public key with its addresses, each carrying the derivation path and index the client used. An empty `addresses` list is a valid state, not an error. `monitoredAt: null` signals an address that never reached the indexer — balances and history for it would be empty, so it is surfaced rather than hidden.

createdAt.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp (seconds).

post.description: Returns per-address balances split by availability, all in satoshis: `spendableSats` (confirmed and unlocked — the only funds that can be spent now), `unconfirmedSats` (outputs of transactions not yet in a block, including our own change), `lockedSats` (outputs reserved by an unfinished `/selfcustody/transaction/build`) and `totalSats`, which is the sum of the three. The buckets never overlap, so they can be displayed side by side. `spendableInUsd` is `null` when a rate is unavailable — that is not a request failure, the satoshi amounts are still exact. Pass `addressId` to narrow to one address.

Forces an out-of-schedule resync of the wallet's addresses. Pass `addressId` to resync one, or `deep: true` to re-read the whole history instead of only new blocks. Results are reported per address: a failure on one address comes back as `ok: false` with an `error` rather than failing the whole request, so a partial refresh is never mistaken for a complete one.

Registers an address the CLIENT derived and starts tracking it on-chain. The server verifies that `address` really derives from `pubkeyHex` and rejects the request otherwise — without that check a wallet could claim someone else's address. The call is idempotent (`created: false` on repeat) and only succeeds once the address is actually being tracked: an untracked address would silently report a zero balance.

Returns recommended fee rates as three tiers (`slow` / `standard` / `fast`) in sat/vByte, sourced from a mempool estimator, with `updatedAt` telling how fresh they are — a cached rate is served when the source is unreachable, and its age is shown rather than hidden. Pass `addressId` AND `amountSats` together to also get `exact`: the fee for that address's real UTXO set, the `inputCount` and `vBytes` behind it, `recipientAmountSats`, and `maxSendableSats`. The last one is what a “Max” button should send — for BTC `fee = feeRate × vBytes` and `vBytes` depends on the input count, which only the server knows.

post.description: Builds an unsigned PSBT for the client to sign locally; the private key never reaches the server. Set `feeIncluded: false` to add the fee on top of `amountSats`, or `true` to take it out of that amount — `recipientAmountSats` reports what the recipient actually receives. Change below the dust threshold is added to the fee instead of creating an unspendable output. The selected outputs are LOCKED until `expiresAt`, so a concurrent build cannot pick the same ones; `quoteId` identifies both the quote and that lock.

toAddress.description: Destination Bitcoin address for the funds.

feeRateSatVb.description: Fee rate in satoshis per virtual byte (sat/vB).

psbtBase64.description: Unsigned transaction as a base64-encoded PSBT (BIP-174). Sign it with the wallet key.

feeSats.description: Network fee for the transaction, in satoshis.

changeSats.description: Change returned to the wallet, in satoshis.

inputCount.description: Number of inputs selected for the transaction.

expiresAt.description: Expiry time as a Unix timestamp (seconds).

post.description: Submits the transaction the client signed and finalized — `rawTx` is signed transaction hex, not a PSBT — and releases the lock on the outputs it spent. Only an unexpired `quoteId` is accepted; past `expiresAt` the quote must be rebuilt. Retrying with the same `rawTx` is safe and returns `wasAlreadySubmitted: true`: the network may have accepted the first attempt while the response never reached the client.

Returns transaction history newest-first with a `nextCursor` for the next page (`null` on the last one); transactions not yet in a block come first. Amounts are stated from the wallet's side: for an incoming transaction what arrived, for an outgoing one what went to recipients excluding our own change. `feeSats` is set only on outgoing transactions — the spender pays the fee — and may be `null` when not all inputs are known to the indexer, since reporting zero there would be wrong. Filter with `statuses` and `directions`.

feeSats.description: Network fee for the transaction, in satoshis.

post.description: Returns one transaction by `txid`, in the same shape as the list entries, including `confirmations`. Use it to follow a send you just broadcast without refetching the whole history — and so that a dropped websocket cannot leave a transfer stuck on “processing” forever.

feeSats.description: Network fee for the transaction, in satoshis.

post.description: Cancels a payment that has not been paid yet — use it when the order is dropped on your side. Only `initiated` and `expired` payments can be canceled; once funds are seen on-chain (`detected`) or confirmed (`paid`) the call fails with `payment_not_cancelable`. Cancelling an already-canceled payment succeeds and changes nothing, so retries are safe. Unlike `expired`, `canceled` is terminal: the watcher stops following the address, so late funds will not flip it to `paid`.

posTerminalLabel.description: Label of the POS terminal (may be null).

posTerminalLocation.description: Location of the POS terminal (may be null).

merchantDisplayName.description: Merchant's public display name (may be null).

btcPriceInUsd.description: BTC/USD price captured when the payment was created.

btcPriceInCurrency.description: BTC price in the payment's `currency`, captured when the payment was created.

currencySymbol.description: Display symbol of the currency, e.g. `$`.

metadata.description: Internal system metadata attached to the payment (reserved; not set by clients).

expiresAt.description: Expiry time as a Unix timestamp (seconds).

qrString.description: Payment encoded as a BIP-21 URI, ready to render as a QR code.

txid.description: On-chain Bitcoin transaction id (hex) of this receipt. Look it up in any block explorer to show the payer their transaction.

amountSats.description: What this transaction paid into **this payment's** address, in satoshis — not the transaction's total, which may pay other outputs as well.

blockHeight.description: Height of the block that included the transaction; `null` while it is still in the mempool.

blockTime.description: Timestamp of that block, Unix seconds; `null` while the transaction is still in the mempool. Historical payments confirmed before this field existed report `null` permanently.

confirmations.description: Confirmations as of **now**, not as of the moment the payment was paid, so the value keeps growing. `0` — seen but not in a block yet. `null` — the current chain tip is not known to us right now, so the count cannot be stated; do not render it as zero, the transaction may well be deeply confirmed. The remaining fields are unaffected.

feeSats.description: Network fee the payer paid for this transaction, in satoshis; `null` when it is not known to us.

transactions.description: On-chain transactions observed paying this payment, freshest first. Empty until something is seen — and empty is a normal state for a payment in `initiated`. More than one element means the payer sent more than one transaction (an overpayment or a top-up); sum `amountSats` across the list to get what actually arrived. Identical for both payment routes: an in-app payment reports its single transaction here just like one paid from an external wallet.

paidAt.description: When the payment was paid, Unix timestamp (seconds); `null` until then. This is the payment's settlement time — for when a single transaction was mined see `transactions[].blockTime`.
